title: Calisthenics Program
warmup: 2 min easy cardio — jog in place, jumping jacks, skipping
Wrists: palms down rocks ×10 · palms up rocks ×10 · fist circles ×10 — before any handstand work
10 bodyweight squats · 10 hip hinges · world's greatest stretch ×5/side
One light set of the first exercise, then a second at half your working load

reference.heading: Double progression
reference.body: Stay at the same variation until you hit the top of the rep range on every set, two sessions in a row. Then add load (backpack) if possible, otherwise move to the harder variation. When you progress, you drop back to the bottom of the range. That's normal. One deliberate exception: Phase 1 pull-ups, which have their own rule written on the exercise.

reference.heading: Supersets
reference.body: Exercises bracketed together alternate. Do one set of the first, wait the shown rest, one set of the second, wait, and repeat. Because the two movements don't compete, each one still gets roughly double the shown rest before its own next set — a 1:30 alternation gives every pull-up set about 3 minutes of recovery. This is what makes the session fit in 45 minutes without shortening anything that matters.

reference.heading: Effort
reference.body: Leave 1–2 reps in the tank on most sets. Going to failure every set on 4 days/week will bury your recovery. The last set of an exercise can go close to failure.

reference.heading: Rest between sets
reference.body: The timer shows the alternation interval, not your recovery. On the paired compound work each movement still gets 2–3 minutes before you repeat it. Don't cut it — short rests are the main reason people get tired quickly and then stall, because you end up limited by fatigue rather than strength, which is the wrong stimulus.

reference.heading: Order
reference.body: Skill work goes first, right after the warm-up, when you're fresh. Never at the end.

reference.heading: Adding the backpack
reference.body: Once you're loading a movement, don't go from the warm-up straight into a working set. Do one set at bodyweight and one at about half your working load first. It costs three minutes and it's the difference between elbows that tolerate weighted pull-ups and elbows that don't.

reference.heading: Advancing phases
reference.body: Never advance by calendar. Advance when you hit every criterion on the phase gate. The gates are the only clock in this program.

reference.heading: Retesting
reference.body: Retest when you think you're close to a gate, not on a schedule. Fresh day, full warm-up, one all-out set of pull-ups, one of dips, one max wall handstand hold. Do the retest instead of that session's first exercise, not on top of it.

reference.heading: Missed a session
reference.body: Take the sessions in order, not by weekday. If you miss Thursday, Upper B is simply what you do next. Never stack two sessions in a day to catch up, and never do the same session twice running to get back on the calendar — the order matters, the weekday doesn't. If you miss a whole week, repeat the last week's loads rather than picking up where the numbers left off.

reference.heading: Deload
reference.body: Every 6–8 weeks, or whenever your numbers go backwards three sessions running at the same load: one week at half the sets, same reps. Keep skill practice. Two bad sessions is noise — sleep, food, a cold bar. Three is a signal. Also deload if poor sleep, achy joints and flat motivation turn up together, whatever the numbers say.

reference.heading: Nutrition — the actual limiting factor
reference.body: At 66 kg, food is what's holding back muscle growth, not training. Eat ~300–400 kcal above maintenance, targeting 0.4–0.7 kg gained per month — about 0.25–0.5% of bodyweight per week. Slower than that and you're leaving most of the result on the table; faster and you're mostly adding fat. If the scale hasn't moved in three weeks, eat more. Protein 110–130 g/day across 3–4 meals. Sleep 7–9 hours.

reference.heading: Progressing a band
reference.body: Bands jump in big steps, so exhaust the small adjustments first: stand wider on the band, then choke up on it, then slow the lowering to 3 seconds. Move to a thicker band only when all three stop working.

reference.heading: Still getting tired quickly after 3 weeks?
reference.body: Breathing and heart rate spiking means conditioning — add two 20–30 min easy walks or rides on off days. Muscles burning out and arms giving up means you're resting too little between sets — time your rests for two weeks and see what changes.

wallHandstand.setup: Hands flat about 10 cm from the wall, shoulder-width, fingers spread and gripping the floor. Walk your feet up until your chest and hips are close to the wall — chest-to-wall, not belly-to-wall.
steps: Push the floor away hard. Shoulders shrugged up towards your ears, elbows locked straight.
Ribs pulled down, glutes squeezed, toes pointed — one straight line from wrists to toes.
Look at the floor between your hands, not at the wall.
Shoulder taps: shift your weight fully onto one hand, tap the opposite shoulder, put it back. Slow, no rush.
mistakes: Arched lower back with the ribs flared. The most common fault, and it's what makes the free-standing hold impossible later.
Bent elbows — the set is over the moment they bend.
Holding to failure. This is skill practice: come down with something left.

handstandNegatives.setup: Chest-to-wall handstand, hands close to the wall. This is a controlled lowering to the top of your head, then a press back up.
steps: From the handstand, bend the elbows slowly and let your head travel forward and down towards the floor.
Touch the top of your head lightly — never crash onto it. Put a folded towel down.
Press back up by driving the floor away, keeping the body line tight.
If you can't press back up yet, do the lowering only and step down.
mistakes: Elbows flaring wide instead of tracking forward.
Letting the hips pike as you descend — the legs should follow the torso, not lead it.

freeHandstand.setup: Away from the wall, on a flat, non-slip surface with room to bail. Learn the bail first: turn your shoulders and step down sideways, don't fold forwards.
steps: Kick up gently — much lighter than feels right. Aim to arrive under balance, not past it.
Balance comes from the fingers: pressing the fingertips down stops you falling over, easing off lets you come back.
Keep the shrug, locked elbows and tight midline from the wall version.
Stack: wrists, shoulders, hips, toes in one line.
mistakes: Kicking too hard and chasing the balance with your back instead of your hands.
Practising when already tired. This goes first in the session for a reason.

pullups.setup: Overhand grip, hands just outside shoulder width. Hang at full stretch with active shoulders — pull the shoulder blades down and back before the arms do anything.
steps: Start each rep from a dead hang, arms straight.
Lead with the elbows, driving them down towards your ribs. Chest towards the bar.
Chin clearly over the bar, then lower under control over about 2 seconds.
Weighted: load the backpack high and tight so it doesn't swing.
mistakes: Kipping — swinging the legs to generate momentum. If the hips move, the rep doesn't count here.
Half reps: not reaching a straight-arm hang at the bottom, or stopping at eyes-to-bar.
Shrugging up into the ears instead of pulling the shoulder blades down.

chinups.setup: Underhand grip, hands about shoulder-width. Same dead hang as the pull-up.
steps: Dead hang, shoulder blades set down and back.
Pull until your chin clears the bar, keeping the elbows close to your sides.
Lower over about 2 seconds to a full straight-arm hang.
mistakes: Letting the elbows drift forward, which turns it into a shoulder movement.
Cutting the bottom short. The stretched position is where most of the growth is.

explosivePullups.setup: Overhand grip, dead hang. The point is bar speed, not rep count — this is muscle-up preparation.
steps: Pull as fast as you physically can from the bottom.
Aim to bring your chest, not your chin, to the bar. Sternum contact is the target.
Lower under control and reset fully between reps.
Stop the set the moment a rep visibly slows — a slow rep trains the wrong thing.
mistakes: Grinding out extra slow reps to finish the set.
Throwing the head back to reach height instead of pulling higher.

pullupNegatives.setup: Jump or step up so your chin starts above the bar. You need a box, a low bar, or a good jump.
steps: Get to the top position with your chin over the bar and chest close to it.
Lower over a full 5 seconds, counting it out.
Fight hardest in the bottom third, where you'll want to drop.
Step or jump back up — never lower and then try to pull out of the hang.
mistakes: A 2-second drop dressed up as a negative. If you can't make 5 seconds, you're doing too many reps.
Relaxing the shoulders at the bottom and dropping into a dead hang.

dips.setup: Parallel bars, arms locked out, shoulders pushed down away from the ears. Slight forward lean of the torso, legs together or crossed behind.
steps: Lower under control until your upper arms are roughly parallel to the floor — shoulders level with the elbows.
Keep the elbows tracking back and fairly close, not flared wide.
Press back to a full lockout without bouncing out of the bottom.
Weighted: bodyweight set first, then half load, then the working sets.
mistakes: Shrugging — letting the shoulders ride up towards the ears at the bottom. This is the main cause of dip shoulder pain.
Going deeper than parallel before your shoulders are ready.
Sitting upright and bouncing. Lean forward slightly and control it.

straightBarDips.setup: A single straight bar at about hip-to-waist height. Start supported on top of the bar, arms locked, wrists over the bar, torso leaning forward over it.
steps: Lean forward so the bar can pass in front of your chest as you descend.
Lower until your chest is near the bar and your upper arms are around parallel.
Press back up and finish leaning slightly over the bar, elbows locked.
This is the top half of a muscle-up. Treat it as skill plus strength.
mistakes: Staying vertical — you'll hit the bar with your chest and have nowhere to go.
Letting the wrists sit behind the bar at the top instead of over it.

bandMuscleups.setup: Loop a band over the bar and put one foot or both knees in it. Overhand grip, thumbs over the bar if you can — it makes the transition much easier.
steps: Explosive pull with a slight backwards swing, aiming chest to bar.
As you reach the top of the pull, drive the chest forward over the bar and roll the wrists over — this is the transition, and it's the whole exercise.
Finish with a straight-bar dip press to lockout.
Lower back down under control rather than dropping off.
mistakes: Chasing reps instead of a clean transition. Three good ones beats ten scrambled.
Staying on a thick band. Drop band thickness as soon as the transition feels smooth.

invertedRows.setup: A bar at about hip height. Hang underneath it, overhand or neutral grip just outside shoulder width, heels on the floor, body in one straight line.
steps: Squeeze glutes and brace the core so the hips don't sag — you're a plank hanging under a bar.
Pull the shoulder blades together first, then bend the elbows.
Touch your chest or lower ribs to the bar and hold for a beat.
Lower until the arms are straight and the shoulder blades come apart.
Feet elevated: heels on a bench or second bar to make it harder.
mistakes: Sagging hips — the most common fault, and it lets you cheat the range.
Pulling with the arms only and never squeezing the shoulder blades.
Shortening the range at the top. Chest to bar or it doesn't count.

invertedRowsElev.setup: Same as the inverted row, with your heels on a bench or box roughly level with the bar so the body is horizontal or better.
steps: Set the line first: heels up, hips lifted, body straight from shoulders to feet.
Pull the shoulder blades together, then the elbows, touching chest or lower ribs to the bar.
Lower to straight arms with the shoulder blades spreading apart.
mistakes: Hips dropping the moment the feet go up — lower the elevation if you can't hold the line.
Bouncing the heels off the bench to start the rep.

pikePushups.setup: Hands and feet on the floor, hips high in an upside-down V. Walk the feet in until your torso is as close to vertical as your hamstrings allow.
steps: Head points at the floor between your hands, hips stay high throughout.
Lower until the crown of your head lightly touches the floor.
Press back up to straight arms without letting the hips drop.
Feet elevated: heels on a chair or step to bring the shoulders more overhead.
mistakes: Turning it into a normal push-up by letting the hips sink — then it's chest, not shoulders.
Lowering the head forward of the hands rather than between them.

pushupsElevated.setup: Feet on a bench or chair, hands slightly wider than shoulders, body in one straight line from heels to head.
steps: Brace the core and squeeze the glutes so the hips don't sag.
Lower over 2 seconds until your chest is just off the floor, elbows at roughly 45° to the body.
Press up in 1 second to full lockout, letting the shoulder blades spread at the top.
mistakes: Elbows flared to 90°, straight out from the shoulders.
Head dropping first, hips second. Everything moves together.
Bouncing off the floor at the bottom.

archerPushups.setup: Push-up position with the hands much wider than normal. One arm will work, the other stays nearly straight and acts as a kickstand.
steps: Lower towards one hand, bending that elbow and keeping the other arm straight out to the side.
Chest comes down close to the working hand.
Press back up through the working arm. Do all reps on one side, then switch — or alternate.
Turn the straight hand's fingers outwards if the shoulder feels pinched.
mistakes: Hips twisting to help. Keep them square to the floor.
Bending the straight arm to share the load, which turns it back into a wide push-up.

bandCurls.setup: Stand on the middle of the band, feet hip-width, a handle or end in each hand, palms forward. Stand wider for more tension.
steps: Elbows pinned to your sides — they don't travel forward.
Curl to full contraction and squeeze at the top, where band tension is highest.
Lower over 2 full seconds against the band rather than letting it snap back.
mistakes: Swinging the torso to start the rep.
Letting the band pull your hands down fast. The lowering is half the exercise.

facePulls.setup: Anchor the band at roughly face height, or loop it around a bar or post. Step back until there's tension with your arms straight out in front. This is a light shoulder-health movement, not a strength lift.
steps: Pull the band towards your face, leading with the elbows and keeping them high — at or above shoulder height.
Finish with your hands beside your ears and the band near your forehead, as if doing a double bicep pose.
Squeeze the shoulder blades together and hold for a beat.
Return slowly to straight arms.
mistakes: Going too heavy and rowing it to the chest with the lats. Lighter band, higher elbows.
Elbows dropping below shoulder height, which turns it into a row.
Chasing reps or load. Keep it at 15 quality reps — it is deliberately not a progression lift.

tuckLsit.setup: Parallel bars, dip bars, or the floor with hands flat beside your hips. Push down hard through straight arms and lift your body clear.
steps: Lock the elbows and push the shoulders down away from the ears — this is what creates the height.
Tuck the knees up towards your chest, thighs around 90° to the torso.
Round the lower back slightly and pull the ribs down. Hold.
On the floor, elevate the hands on books or blocks if you can't clear your feet yet.
mistakes: Shrugged shoulders and bent elbows — the two together make the hold impossible.
Leaning back to keep the knees up instead of compressing the hips.

tuckLsitAdv.setup: Same as the tuck L-sit, but the thighs now come up to horizontal with the knees still bent at 90°, shins parallel to the floor.
steps: Set the depression first: elbows locked, shoulders pushed down.
Bring the thighs to parallel with the floor and hold the shins level.
Keep the lower back flat rather than arched — you should feel this in the hip flexors and abs.
mistakes: Letting the thighs drop back towards a normal tuck as the hold gets hard. Stop the set instead.
Holding your breath. Breathe shallowly and steadily.

fullLsit.setup: From the advanced tuck, straighten one leg fully while the other stays tucked. Alternate which leg extends between sets.
steps: Elbows locked, shoulders pushed down, hips as high as you can get them.
Extend one leg straight out, toes pointed, held at or above hip height.
Keep the tucked knee at 90° rather than letting it drift down.
Hold, then swap legs on the next set.
mistakes: Extending the leg but letting the whole body sink — height first, then extension.
Only ever training one side.

pikeCompression.setup: Sit on the floor with your legs straight out in front, hands flat on the floor beside your hips. Sit tall — don't lean back.
steps: Push into the floor with your hands and pull the toes back towards you.
Lift both heels off the floor using the hip flexors. Even a centimetre counts.
Hold for a second at the top, lower under control.
Keep the knees locked straight the whole time.
mistakes: Leaning back to make the lift easier. That's the exact cheat the L-sit won't allow.
Bending the knees. Straight legs or it isn't training compression.

hollowHold.setup: Lie on your back, arms overhead, legs straight. Press your lower back flat into the floor before you lift anything — this is the whole exercise.
steps: Pull the ribs down towards the hips and flatten the lumbar spine.
Lift the shoulder blades and legs off the floor, keeping that flat back.
Point the toes, squeeze everything, and breathe shallowly.
Too hard? Bend the knees or bring the arms to your sides — never let the back arch.
mistakes: A gap under the lower back. If you can slide a hand under, raise the legs higher until you can't.
Straining the neck. Keep the chin slightly tucked and look at your knees.

sidePlank.setup: Lie on your side, forearm on the floor with the elbow directly under the shoulder. Legs stacked, feet on top of each other.
steps: Lift the hips until your body is one straight line from ankle to head.
Keep the hips stacked vertically — don't let the top hip roll forward or back.
Push the bottom shoulder away from the floor rather than sinking into it.
Easier version: bottom knee bent and on the floor.
mistakes: Hips sagging towards the floor as the set goes on.
Rotating towards the floor, which turns it back into a front plank.

kneeRaises.setup: Dead hang from the bar, overhand grip, shoulders active — pulled down, not slumped into the joints.
steps: Kill any swing before the first rep.
Raise the knees to at least hip height, curling the pelvis up slightly at the top.
Lower slowly and under control — do not let the legs fall.
Pause a beat at the bottom if you start swinging.
mistakes: Using a swing to throw the knees up. Slow beats high.
Only lifting the knees without any pelvic curl, which leaves the lower abs out of it.

legRaises.setup: Dead hang, active shoulders, legs straight and together. This is the knee raise with the knees locked.
steps: No swing. Brace before the first rep.
Raise straight legs to at least hip height — towards the bar if you can.
Point the toes and keep the knees locked throughout.
Lower over 2–3 seconds under full control.
mistakes: Bending the knees as it gets hard. Drop back to knee raises instead.
Dropping the legs. The lowering is where the strength comes from.

bulgarian.setup: Stand about a stride in front of a bench, chair or step. Put the top of one foot on it behind you. The front foot should be far enough forward that the knee stays over the mid-foot at the bottom.
steps: Torso slightly forward, chest up, front foot flat.
Lower straight down until the front thigh is around parallel and the back knee is close to the floor.
Drive up through the front heel. The back leg is balance, not power.
Weighted: backpack on your back, or hold it to your chest for better balance.
mistakes: Standing too close to the bench, which jams the front knee forward and hurts.
Pushing off the back foot to help.
Finding the balance with the set. Steady yourself with a fingertip on a wall if you need to.

stepUps.setup: A box, bench or step at roughly knee height. Stand facing it, one whole foot on the surface.
steps: Shift your weight over the top foot, chest up.
Stand up by pushing through that heel — no pushing off, no hopping with the bottom foot.
Stand fully tall at the top, then lower over 2–3 seconds under control.
The bottom foot touches the floor lightly; it never takes the load.
mistakes: Pushing off the trailing leg, which is what turns this into a jump.
Dropping back down instead of lowering. Half the point is the lowering.

pistolAssisted.setup: Hold a pole, door frame or low bar for balance, or stand in front of a bench you can sit back to. Stand on one leg with the other extended in front.
steps: Sit back and down slowly, keeping the free leg off the floor and the heel of the standing foot planted.
Use the hands only for balance and the minimum assistance you need.
Go as deep as you can control — a bench behind you gives a consistent depth to aim for.
Drive back up through the whole foot.
mistakes: Pulling yourself up with the arms. They're a kickstand, not a rope.
The standing heel lifting off the floor. Work on ankle mobility or elevate the heel slightly.

pistolSquats.setup: Stand on one leg, other leg straight out in front, arms out for counterbalance. Nothing to hold.
steps: Lower slowly, sitting back and keeping the free leg off the floor throughout.
Go all the way down until the hamstring meets the calf.
Keep the standing heel down and the chest up.
Drive back up without rocking or bouncing out of the bottom.
mistakes: Bouncing out of the bottom, which is how knees get irritated.
The free leg touching down to help.
Rushing back to full pistols after a layoff. Drop to assisted.

slRdl.setup: Stand on one leg, a soft bend in that knee. The other leg will travel straight back as a counterweight.
steps: Hinge at the hip — push the hips backwards, don't bend at the waist.
Let the torso and back leg move together like a see-saw until the torso is near horizontal.
Back flat throughout, shoulders square to the floor.
Feel the stretch in the standing hamstring, then drive the hips forward to stand up.
Weighted: hold the backpack in the opposite hand to the standing leg.
mistakes: Squatting instead of hinging — if the knee travels forward, it's a squat.
Rounding the lower back at the bottom.
The hips rotating open. Keep both hip bones pointing at the floor.

nordics.setup: Kneel on something soft with your ankles anchored — under a sofa, a loaded bar, or a partner holding them. Body straight from knees to head.
steps: Hands up in front of your chest, ready to catch yourself.
Lower forwards as slowly as you possibly can, resisting the whole way with the hamstrings.
Catch yourself with your hands when you lose control, then push back to the start.
Full Nordics: pull yourself back up with the hamstrings using no more than a light push.
mistakes: Breaking at the hips. Keep a straight line from knees to shoulders — this is the single most common fault.
Dropping fast. If you can't slow it down, reduce range or add more of a hand push.

calfRaise.setup: Ball of one foot on the edge of a step, heel hanging free. Hold something for balance. The other foot is off the step.
steps: Drop the heel as far below the step as your ankle allows and pause in the stretch.
Push up onto the ball of the foot as high as you can and squeeze for a second at the top.
Lower over 2–3 seconds back into the stretch.
Weighted: backpack on.
mistakes: Short, bouncy reps at the top. The full stretch at the bottom is where this works.
Bending the knee to help. Keep it straight.

skills.name: Muscle-up
skills.goal: One clean rep on the bar

phases.name: Phase 1
phases.span: Where you start. Leave when you clear the Phase 2 gate, however long that takes.

exercises.name: Wall handstand
exercises.note: Chest to wall. Stop before failure — this is practice, not a set.

exercises.name: Pull-ups
exercises.note: Exception to the progression rule: don't wait for all six sets. Add one rep to one set each week — 2,2,2,2,2,2 → 3,2,2,2,2,2 → 3,3,2,2,2,2. At 6×3, retest your max. Six clean doubles beats three ugly fives.

exercises.name: Dips
exercises.note: Full range, controlled.

exercises.name: Inverted rows
exercises.note: Park bar at hip height. Squeeze at the top.

exercises.name: Pike push-ups
exercises.note: Elevate the feet once this gets easy.

exercises.name: Band curls
exercises.note: Elbows pinned to your sides. 2 seconds down.

exercises.name: Band face pulls
exercises.note: Elbows high, hands finish beside your ears. Not a progression lift — keep it at 15 quality reps.

exercises.name: Tuck L-sit
exercises.note: On dip bars or the floor.

exercises.name: Bulgarian split squat
exercises.note: Load the backpack once you pass 12.

exercises.name: Hanging knee raises
exercises.note: No swinging.

exercises.name: Step-ups
exercises.note: Knee height. Slow, no pushing off the back foot.

exercises.name: Hollow body hold
exercises.note: Lower back stays pressed down.

exercises.name: Single-leg calf raise
exercises.note: Full stretch at the bottom.

exercises.name: Wall handstand + shoulder taps
exercises.note: Add the taps once the hold is solid.

exercises.name: Dips
exercises.note: Heavier day — this is the one to load first.

exercises.name: Chin-ups
exercises.note: Underhand. Easier than pull-ups — that's the point.

exercises.name: Push-ups, feet elevated
exercises.note: 2 seconds down, 1 up.

exercises.name: Pull-up negatives
exercises.note: Jump up, lower over 5 s. This is what builds the pull-up at your level.

exercises.name: Band face pulls
exercises.note: Shoulder health and rear delts. Against this much pressing, it isn't optional.

exercises.name: Seated pike leg lifts
exercises.note: Sit legs straight, hands by your hips, lift the heels off the floor. Compression is what actually gates the L-sit, not core strength.

exercises.name: Single-leg Romanian deadlift
exercises.note: Hinge at the hip, back flat, feel the hamstring. Hold the backpack in the opposite hand once bodyweight is easy.

exercises.name: Side plank
exercises.note: Hips stacked and lifted. The only anti-rotation work in the program.

exercises.name: Nordic curl negatives
exercises.note: Lower as slowly as you can, push back up with your hands.

phases.name: Phase 2
phases.span: Starts when you clear the Phase 2 gate.

exercises.name: Wall handstand
exercises.note: Chest to wall. Three long holds, not four short ones. The Phase 3 gate is 60 s, so the range runs to it.

exercises.name: Pull-ups
exercises.note: Normal double progression now. Once you clear 5 on every set, start adding backpack weight.

exercises.name: Dips
exercises.note: Add backpack weight when you clear 12.

exercises.name: Advanced tuck L-sit
exercises.note: Hips open more than a plain tuck.

exercises.name: Hanging straight leg raises
exercises.note: No swinging.

exercises.name: Assisted pistol squat
exercises.note: Box squat, to a lower and lower surface.

exercises.name: Wall handstand negatives
exercises.note: Walk in close, lower slowly to your head, press back up.

exercises.name: Dips
exercises.note: Heavier day — load this one first.

phases.name: Phase 3
phases.span: Starts when you clear the Phase 3 gate. The muscle-up becomes reasonable here.

exercises.name: Free-standing handstand
exercises.note: Kick-up practice against the wall, then away from it.

exercises.name: Explosive pull-ups
exercises.note: Chest to bar. Speed, not grind — stop the set the moment a rep slows down.

exercises.name: Weighted pull-ups
exercises.note: This is where most of the muscle comes from now.

exercises.name: Straight-bar dips
exercises.note: Harder than parallel bars, and the muscle-up needs them.

exercises.name: L-sit, one leg straight
exercises.note: One leg straight, then both.

exercises.name: Band-assisted muscle-ups
exercises.note: Focus on the transition, not the rep. Drop band thickness to progress.
